_comment: Site registry per docs/03. Deployment records are REQUIRED before project-sensor ingest (docs/06 registry gate). window_local values below are from the reviewed Tidbit deployment; verify before first real run. series_map keys are the sensor name as it appears in the vendor file header ('Tidbit 1 , degF' -> 'Tidbit 1'), not the full column label; values are controlled parameter names from parameters.json. measured_parameters on a public station lists the controlled parameters that station actually carries an instrument for; a fetcher stores only those, so a fixed-column format cannot land rows for a sensor the station does not have. Omit it only while nobody has checked - an absent field means undeclared, and the fetcher stores everything it recognises and says so. site_id and a deployment's depth_m are both part of the storage dedupe key, so both are IMMUTABLE once rows for that deployment have landed in observations/ - editing either leaves the old rows behind under the old key, nothing raises, and one instrument becomes two series (docs/03 'Partition files and idempotence'). Correcting window_local is not in this class and is safe: it moves qc_flag, not the key. sensor_depths_m takes a number when the registry supplies the depth and a LIST when the payload does - a moored string measures one parameter at many depths, so the list records which depths have been seen rather than a value the fetcher writes (docs/03 'A source may be self-describing on depth'). For an ERDDAP-served station, station_code is the pinned dataset ID: it is the identifier the provider knows the station by, which is what a fetcher asks for. A hand-downloaded station carries an `archive` block pinning which cumulative snapshot its landings came from - the Kelp Watch revision pin applied to a site - and an ingest refuses without one; `archive.archived` is also the raw landing directory, so two snapshots of one record cannot interleave (docs/03).

sites.name: TidbiT 1 site (yellow buoy)

deployments.notes: depth_m is the logger depth, reported by the placer as 27 fsw and converted at 0.3048 m/ft. fsw here is feet of depth as a dive computer displays it, not the 1/33 atm pressure unit, which would give 8.27 m.

sites.notes: Position surveyed and supplied by the placer 2026-08-27, superseding the conflicting reports ~1-2 km apart this record previously carried and the null it held while they stood. WGS84, converted from 32 deg 51' 08.2" N, 117 deg 16' 10.1" W. Position is a site fact, not a deployment one: a redeployment of this logger at another spot is a new site record, not another deployments[] entry here.

sites.name: TidbiT 2 site

deployments.notes: series_map key is 'Temperature', the name in this file's column header - the logger's series name was left at the factory default, so it is NOT 'Tidbit 2'. window_local is PROVISIONAL and derived from the record itself, not from a dive log: the first four samples read 21.2-22.2 degC on deck, 07:40 reads 14.8 degC and it stays down, settling only 0.4 degC over the next 20 minutes, so the logger was in and near-equilibrated by 07:40. At the other end there is nothing to exclude - Host Connected and End of File share 08:36:48, so it was stopped the instant it was connected and never warmed; the last sample is 08:30 at 15.6 degC. Confirm against the dive log and correct here: a corrected window is a registry edit plus a rebuild, and excluded rows are flagged (qc_flag 4), never deleted. Do not trust the same derivation on a shallow logger: PROJ:TIDBIT-1's window came from the placer's own hand-edited file, and a first-cold-reading rule would have picked its 07:40 dunk and been wrong by two samples. Cost if this window is wrong by a sample: min/mean/max do not move (13.12/16.50/23.02 degC either way), but threshold and spell features do - all four on-deck rows are >= 20 degC and they set 11 Jul's daily maximum to 22.18 degC where the water reached 20.36 degC. depth_m is the logger depth, reported by the placer as 55 fsw and converted at 0.3048 m/ft; the 1/33 atm pressure definition would give 16.85 m.

sites.notes: Position surveyed and supplied by the placer 2026-08-27. WGS84, as given in decimal degrees. Its own site rather than a second deployments[] entry on PROJ:TIDBIT-1: it sits 455 m from that logger and 8.5 m deeper, and position is a site fact that Deployment cannot carry by construction. Corroborated by the data - over the span the two records share (11 Jul 08:00 to 1 Aug 07:30 local, 3,022 samples each) this logger averaged 17.42 degC against 21.58 degC at PROJ:TIDBIT-1, which is what sitting below the thermocline looks like and is why the two cannot share a record. neighbor_refs names NDBC:LJAC1 and COOPS:9410230 because that platform is the nearest public station, not because it is depth-comparable: its only sea_water_temperature sensor sits 3.4 m below MLLW, 13.4 m above this logger and above the summer thermocline. Over 13 Jul - 1 Aug 2026, where LJAC1's record in observations/ overlaps this deployment, that reference averaged 22.56 degC against this logger's 17.42 degC. Reporting that ~5 degC gap as instrument bias would invert what docs/04's neighbor validation table is evidence for, so bias and RMSE are NOT reportable for this site; correlation is, labelled with the depth gap. PROJ:TIDBIT-1 at 8.23 m does not carry the caveat - the same reference sits 4.8 m above it and the offset there is about 1 degC. See docs/04 'Neighbor validation'.

sites.name: La Jolla shore station (NDBC)
sites.notes: Sensor geometry from the NDBC station page, retrieved 2026-08-25: sea temp depth 3.4 m below MLLW; air temp 7.2 m and anemometer 8.2 m above a site elevation of 9.3 m above MSL. The 3.4 m intake is why depth_m is recorded per parameter - comparing it to a logger at another depth is the error docs/02 says to prevent structurally. NOT an independent station from COOPS:9410230: the NDBC station page titles this platform 'LJAC1 - 9410230 - La Jolla, CA', owned by NOAA NOS. NDBC redistributes the NOS observations, so the two site records describe one instrument package and must never both count as neighbors for the same validation. measured_parameters omits the wave parameters because this shore station has no wave sensor: the stdmet format carries WVHT and DPD in every file, and across the 2007-2025 archive plus realtime all 3,289,004 wave rows are the sentinel, with exactly one distinct value in each column of the landed 2023 file (87,302 records). Wave data for this location comes from CDIP, not from here.

sites.name: La Jolla (Scripps Pier) tide station
sites.notes: Same NOS platform as NDBC:LJAC1 - see that record. Water level here is the product CO-OPS serves with an explicit datum (MLLW, docs/03); NDBC's TIDE column for the same platform declares no datum and is deliberately not ingested.

sites.name: La Jolla, Scripps Pier (SIO Shore Stations)

archive.citation: Carter, Melissa L.; Flick, Reinhard E.; Terrill, Eric; Beckhaus, Elena C.; Martin, Kayla; Fey, Connie L.; Walker, Patricia W.; Largier, John L.; McGowan, John A. (2022). Shore Stations Program - La Jolla, Scripps Pier (La Jolla Archive, 2026-06-30). In Shore Stations Program Data Archive: Current and Historical Coastal Ocean Temperature and Salinity Measurements from California Stations. UC San Diego Library Digital Collections. https://doi.org/10.6075/J06T0K0M. Funding for the Shore Stations Program provided by the California Department of Parks and Recreation, Natural Resources Division, Award# C22820005.

sites.notes: Position 32.866944, -117.257139 converted from the 32 deg 52' 01.0" N 117 deg 15' 25.7" W the archive prints in its own header, identical across all fourteen downloaded snapshots. It is read from the file at every ingest and compared against this record, which is how a dropped archive is matched to a site at all: unlike a Kelp Watch export, this file says which station it describes, so the identification is evidence rather than a filename convention. station_code is the program's own name for the station and the prefix its files arrive under; there is nothing to fetch with it. sensor_depths_m takes the LIST form because surface and bottom are two series sharing every row and the file declares both nominal depths in its title line - the registry checks them rather than supplying them (docs/03 'A source may be self-describing on depth'). The ~ is the program's own and neither depth is better than +/-0.5 m: the bottom figure is a sounding at a fixed pier platform, not a sensor depth. They land as 0.5 and 5.0 and are permanent, since depth_m is part of the storage key. The bottom series begins 1926-07-21, ten years after the surface one. archive pins the snapshot these landings came from; the file declares its own archive date, so a file from another snapshot is quarantined rather than landed under this pin. Bump it deliberately: each download is a cumulative snapshot of the whole 110-year record, so a new one is a rewrite rather than an append. The citation is pinned here rather than in a document because the funding award number differs between snapshots - the five oldest name C1670003. NOT same_platform_as NDBC:LJAC1 or COOPS:9410230 despite sitting about 10 m from that platform: this is a hand-taken bottle at 0.5 m and 5 m against an automated NOS sensor 3.4 m below MLLW, so they are co-located rather than one instrument, and the agreement between them is evidence rather than an identity - bias -0.07 degC, RMSE 1.02, r 0.918 over 5,822 overlapping days 2007-2025 at 5 m, against +0.66 degC bias at 0.5 m. docs/04 has no way to say co-located-but-not-the-same, which is https://github.com/cweber12/kelp-compare/issues/69. Not a neighbor_ref for either project logger: this record ends 2026-03-31 and both deployments begin July 2026, so there is nothing to compare. One daily grab sample, not a continuous series: threshold and spell features are comparable to a moored sensor's, p95 and variance are not. The QARTOD thresholds in parameters.json are tuned for a 10-minute logger and misfire here, so do not run kelpcompare qc over this source yet - https://github.com/cweber12/kelp-compare/issues/68. Temperature only; the same download ships LaJolla_SALT_* and salinity has no parameters.json entry.

sites.name: Point Loma Ocean Outfall RTOMS mooring
sites.notes: Position 32.66996, -117.32676 taken from the CeNCOOS ERDDAP dataset and verified 2026-08-28 to be internally consistent: the dataset's geospatial_lat/lon attributes and the latitude/longitude columns of the rows themselves give the same pair, and it agrees with the depth the string reaches - 90 m off a Point Loma outfall terminus at about 94 m. That check is not ceremony: the sibling south-bay-ocean-outfall-historic dataset gives three different answers for where its instrument was, so a position from this provider is corroborated before it is recorded (docs/02 'City of San Diego RTOMS'). The mooring is a watch-circle buoy and its instantaneous position moves with the current; this is the nominal anchor position the provider publishes, not a GPS fix. sensor_depths_m lists the 11 depths carrying sea_water_temperature on this feed, read from the rows where that variable is not null - the dataset's z axis takes far more values than this because it is a TimeSeriesProfile that flattens the ADCP's 1 m velocity bins onto the same axis. 9 m and 10 m are both here and are the same physical position on the string across two deployments; they land as two series rather than being rounded together, because depth_m is part of the storage key and permanent. The distance this note used to claim - 25 km from the La Jolla beds - was an estimate made when every polygon carried a null geometry, and the recorded outlines falsify it. Measured in UTM 11N to the nearest point on each outline, the basis the polygon registry's other distance claims use and one geodesic distances agree with to within 9 m: 14763 m to KELP:LA-JOLLA, 20911 m to the nearer project sensor, 22800 m station-to-station to NDBC:LJAC1 - and 5264 m to KELP:SAN-DIEGO, the bed the old note never measured against. That makes it the nearest site of any kind to that bed: the next is PROJ:TIDBIT-1 at 11892 m, the next public station SDRTOMS:SBOO at 13024 m, and SIO:LAJOLLA-PIER - the reference this bed is actually paired with - 13535 m, two and a half times further. NOT a neighbor_ref, and the record decides that rather than the range: it ends 2024-12-09 and both project deployments begin July 2026, so there is nothing to compare. Its absence from every polygon's site_ids has no distance argument left behind it and rests on the diffuser alone - the mooring sits on a wastewater outfall terminus, so whether the water it measures represents the bed's is a real question about representativeness rather than about range. Deciding that is the pairing rule in https://github.com/cweber12/kelp-compare/issues/86 and not this note; note also that on the current 2007-2019 climatology baseline every anomaly from this record is null (docs/02), so a pairing made today would add rows and no signal.

sites.name: South Bay Ocean Outfall RTOMS mooring
sites.notes: Position 32.53171, -117.18631, verified on the same basis as SDRTOMS:PLOO on 2026-08-28 - attributes and row columns agree, and the 26 m string depth matches the shallower South Bay outfall. Its 2020-01 to 2022-11 history is NOT ingested: that window lives only in south-bay-ocean-outfall-historic, which claims Point Loma's coordinates in its metadata, La Jolla's in its own latitude/longitude columns, and South Bay's in its depth range. The depths are the only one of the three matching the title, so the data is probably this mooring's and both positions are wrong - but that is a guess, and position is a reviewed fact here, so the window is left out until the provider fixes it (docs/02). Coverage therefore starts 2021-11-03 and runs to 2025-06-04. sensor_depths_m lists the 6 depths carrying sea_water_temperature, read from the non-null rows; 25 m and 26 m, and 18 m and 20 m, are deployment-to-deployment drift on the same positions and land as separate series. The ~15 km to KELP:IMPERIAL-BEACH this note used to claim was an estimate made when every polygon carried a null geometry. Measured in UTM 11N against the recorded outline it is 2968 m, geodesic 2969 m - the closest any public station comes to any bed except La Jolla. The next site of any kind is SDRTOMS:PLOO at 17629 m, nearly six times further, and the nearest reference this bed is actually paired with, SIO:LAJOLLA-PIER, is 32313 m - eleven times further. It is 13024 m from KELP:SAN-DIEGO and 30813 m from KELP:LA-JOLLA. NOT a neighbor_ref, and the record decides that rather than the range: coverage ends 2025-06-04 and both project deployments begin July 2026, so there is nothing to compare. Its absence from KELP:IMPERIAL-BEACH's site_ids now rests on the diffuser alone - the mooring sits on a wastewater outfall, so whether it measures the bed's water is a real question about representativeness rather than about range - and unlike the neighbor_ref question the date gap does not dispose of it, because docs/04 s4.5 compares a station against the kelp record rather than against a logger. That pairing is https://github.com/cweber12/kelp-compare/issues/86; what constrains it today is that on the current 2007-2019 climatology baseline every anomaly from this record is null (docs/02).

sites.name: Scripps Nearshore (NDBC 46254)
sites.notes: Waverider buoy, position and sensor geometry from NDBC's published station_table.txt and station page, retrieved 2026-08-30: sea temp depth 0.46 m below the water line, water depth 46 m. That 0.46 m is a SURFACE measurement and the reason depth is recorded per parameter - NDBC:LJAC1 measures at 3.4 m and SIO:LAJOLLA-PIER at 0.5 m and 5.0 m, and the project loggers sit at 8.23 m and 16.76 m, so this is the shallowest reference in the registry and 7.8 m above PROJ:TIDBIT-1. Nearest-point distance to KELP:LA-JOLLA is 1396 m in EPSG:32611, nearer than either reference that bed is currently paired with (SIO:LAJOLLA-PIER 1718 m, NDBC:LJAC1 1731 m), which is what makes it matter for docs/04 s4.5. NOT paired into any polygon here: which polygon a station joins follows the pairing rule https://github.com/cweber12/kelp-compare/issues/86 owns, and this record deliberately does not invent a second one - the same placed-but-unpaired state SDRTOMS:PLOO and SDRTOMS:SBOO are in. Reports only WVHT DPD APD MWD WTMP; every other stdmet column is sentinel in both layouts, checked against the realtime feed and the 2024 archive. APD and MWD are carried but have no controlled name in parameters.json and are deliberately not invented here (https://github.com/cweber12/kelp-compare/issues/97). The wave parameters declared here have a valid_range but no QARTOD spike or rate_of_change block, so their QC is weaker than sea_water_temperature's until that is tuned (https://github.com/cweber12/kelp-compare/issues/97, and https://github.com/cweber12/kelp-compare/issues/68 on cadence). Archive begins 2015-02-12 and runs to 2025, which is inside but does not span the 2007-2019 climatology baseline: on the canonical window every anomaly from this record is null, and it would need a declared baseline override to carry one at all (docs/04 s3, ADR-007). Not backfilled yet.

sites.name: Del Mar Nearshore (NDBC 46266)
sites.notes: Waverider buoy, position and sensor geometry from NDBC's published station_table.txt and station page, retrieved 2026-08-30: sea temp depth 0.46 m below the water line, water depth 17 m. This buoy sits INSIDE the KELP:DEL-MAR outline - nearest-point distance 0 m in EPSG:32611 - so it is not a neighbour in the docs/04 s1 sense at all but a measurement of the water that bed's canopy is in. The bed is currently paired with NDBC:LJAC1 at 8574 m. NOT paired into any polygon here for the same reason as NDBC:46254: the pairing rule is https://github.com/cweber12/kelp-compare/issues/86. Reports only WVHT DPD APD MWD WTMP; every other stdmet column is sentinel in both layouts, checked against the realtime feed and the 2024 archive. APD and MWD have no controlled name and are not invented here; the declared wave parameters have no QARTOD spike or rate_of_change block yet (https://github.com/cweber12/kelp-compare/issues/97). Archive begins 2019-12-06 - the 2019 file is 1205 rows covering 6-31 December, not a year - so the record is effectively 2020 onward and holds six complete years against a min_years of 10. It therefore post-dates the 2007-2019 baseline entirely and cannot carry an anomaly under any declared window until 2030, which is the rule working rather than an exception to carve (docs/04 s3, ADR-007). Not backfilled yet.
